title: Curiosity Surveys the Boxwork Region
summary: Curiosity's Mastcam panorama shows low boxwork ridges with hollows between them. NASA describes the formations as the result of water leaking through rock cracks, minerals hardening in those cracks, and later wind erosion removing softer rock. The panorama combines 179 images acquired on 2025-09-26.
limitations: A published interpretation of observed morphology; not a spatially complete subsurface hydrology model or a navigation hazard map.

title: Curiosity Studies Nodules on Boxwork Formations
summary: Curiosity's Mars Hand Lens Imager photographed pea-sized nodules in the boxwork region. NASA describes the mosaic as 50 images taken at five locations, with ten focus settings at each location. NASA says the nodules were formed by minerals left behind as groundwater dried billions of years ago.
limitations: The image is close-range and local to sampled camera fields. It does not establish that nodules are present everywhere in the region.

title: NASA's Curiosity Rover Sees Martian Spiderwebs Up Close
summary: NASA/JPL reports that the boxwork ridges are roughly 1 to 2 metres tall with sandy hollows between them. The formations suggest ancient groundwater flowed in this part of Mount Sharp later than scientists expected. The article reports that dark lines previously identified from orbit were found by Curiosity to be fractures, supporting a proposed groundwater pathway interpretation.
limitations: The article summarizes the mission team's interpretation. It does not provide a gridded digital elevation model or astronaut-scale traversability classification.

title: Curiosity Views Boxwork Patterns at a Distance
summary: Curiosity's Mastcam panorama shows low ridges identified as boxwork patterns. NASA describes them as thought to have formed through groundwater moving through rock cracks, with minerals strengthening some areas before wind erosion exposed the resistant ridges.
limitations: A rover panorama with local scene context; not a global geological classification layer.

title: PDS Geosciences Node: Mars Science Laboratory Archive
instrument: APXS, ChemCam, CheMin, DAN, SAM, REMS, RAD and related archives
summary: The PDS Geosciences Node lists instrument archives for Curiosity. REMS data are archived at the PDS Atmospheres Node and RAD data at the PDS Planetary Plasma Interactions Node. The archive publishes instrument data in release cycles and product formats vary by instrument and processing level.
credit: NASA Planetary Data System Geosciences Node
limitations: Use the relevant instrument product label and SIS for field definitions, calibration, units, timestamps and rover location.
